question: Which traditional dance from Uttar Pradesh involves women carrying lighted oil lamps on their heads?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charkula**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charkula** is a spectacular folk dance that originated in the **Braj region** of **Western Uttar Pradesh**, an area deeply associated with the legends of **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed by women to celebrate the birth of **Radha**, the consort of **Lord Krishna**, specifically on the third day after **Holi** (known as **Dooj**).
 
• Performers balance a heavy, multi-tiered circular wooden pyramid called a **Charkula** on their heads; this structure typically holds exactly **108 lighted oil lamps** (diyas) arranged in tiers.
 
• The wooden structure can weigh between **40 to 50 kilograms**, and dancers must maintain perfect balance while moving to the rhythmic beats of **Nagada** (drums) and **Rasiya** folk songs.
 
• Legend suggests that **Radha’s grandmother** ran out of her house with a chariot wheel on her head to announce **Radha’s birth**, which eventually evolved into this unique lamp-balancing dance form.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raslila**:
 
 
• A major dance-drama form from the **Braj region** of **Uttar Pradesh**, depicting the divine love and childhood pranks of **Lord Krishna** and the **Gopis**.
 
• It is an integral part of festivals like **Janmashtami** and is performed in sacred towns like **Mathura** and **Vrindavan**.
 
 
 
• **Giddha**:
 
 
• A high-energy, traditional folk dance from the state of **Punjab**, performed exclusively by **women** during festive or social occasions like **Teeyan**.
 
• It is characterized by the singing of **Boliyan** (couplets) and rhythmic clapping, reflecting the grace and vibrant spirit of Punjabi culture.
 
 
 
• **Bhangra**:
 
 
• One of the most popular folk dances of **Punjab**, traditionally performed by men to celebrate the **Vaisakhi** harvest festival.
 
• It involves athletic movements and is performed to the powerful beat of the **Dhol** drum.
